_comment: DESIGN.md §9. Twelve normal monsters spanning all four armor types, plus four bosses - one per armor type, drawn at random on boss waves (§3.4). Six of the twelve carry an ability and six do not: a wave whose every member is special is a wave with nothing special in it, so the cheap bodies stay cheap and the ones worth recognising are the ones a defence has to answer differently. Every boss has one, and three of the four are thresholds - wounding it is what sets it off. `range` is reach measured EDGE TO EDGE, so a melee value near zero means walking up and touching. `bodyRadius` is both the collision size and the drawn size. All placeholders. WAVE MONSTERS ARE ONE STRENGTH. Every wave from 1 to 19 that is not a boss wave is a single armor/damage combination (waves.json `combinations`), drawn at random, so the sixteen monsters that make those waves are stated to one strength - hp times damage per second about 270 at a scale of 1, less for one whose ability or reach makes it harder - each split between health and damage the way that monster was: a Carapace is all shell, a Swarmling all teeth. The wave table (`scale`) grows them all alike.

monsters.name: Swarmling
monsters._note: THE EARLY BLAST, under the first damage chart (when Blast was what Flesh feared). The chart is now one cycle and Arcane is what Flesh fears; every armor/damage pair has a wave of its own (waves.json), so no armor is safe for long.

monsters.name: Stalker
monsters._note: Blast, not Pierce, since the wave-6-to-10 sweep. Pierce was the damage type of every heavy hitter in the monster set - Warden, Carapace and this - while Blast belonged to the Swarmling and the Bloater, one tiny and one rare. So Flesh, which only Blast hurts, was the best armor to wear for the whole first half of the game, and the builder whose cheap front line wears it (Pyre) was first or near-first at every wave. The rush wave is where Flesh fronts now pay for it.

monsters.name: Spitter
monsters._note: THE RANGED MONSTER. Every other monster in the game fights from 0.9 tiles or closer, so a front line only ever had to stand in the way. A Spitter stops two and a half tiles short and shoots over it, which means a line that does not walk forward to meet it is a line being shot for free, and a back line that out-ranges it is worth more than one that out-damages it. Frail on purpose: it is a thing to be reached.

monsters.name: Mite
monsters._note: THE SMALL ONE. Every monster used to be the same 0.22-tile disc, so the same six or seven could stand around a unit whatever the wave was. A Mite is 0.13 - small enough that nearly three times as many fit in the same ring - and the fastest thing in the game, so it arrives in the gaps before the line has closed them. One is nothing; forty surrounding a gun are the whole wave. Splash is the answer, and so is a line with no gaps in it.

monsters.name: Mender
monsters._note: THE HEALER. Stops short like a Spitter and spends the fight closing the worst wound on the monster in front of it, a twentieth of that body's health every two and a half seconds. A wave with Menders in it is a wave where killing things is not enough: the answer is reach, or a diver, or burst that finishes a body between two heals. Revenants are immune to it, as they are to everything.

monsters.name: Herald
monsters._note: SENT, never spawned by a wave (sends.json). Carries the pack's standard: everything around it marches and swings faster. Worth sending late, when the pack around it is a wave-20 pack.

monsters.name: Bastion
monsters._note: SENT, never spawned by a wave. A walking tower that nothing near can be slowed, rooted or stunned: the answer to a line built on control, bought by the player being held by one.

monsters.name: Behemoth
monsters._note: SENT, never spawned by a wave. The top of the send ladder: the most body a gem buys, and it stamps on whatever stands in front of it. Opens at wave 10 (sends.json `_unlock`).

bosses.name: Brood Sire
bosses._note: §3.4, amended. The bank is FOUR BODIES OF EQUAL POWER in four armor types, not a difficulty ladder: a boss is drawn at random, so a bank whose members ran 1,400 to 3,100 HP made wave 5 a different fight depending on the die. What makes wave 25's boss harder than wave 5's is waves.bossScaling, applied per BOSS WAVE. They still differ in shape - the ward one hits hardest and has least health, the flesh one the reverse - so which comes up changes how you fight it and not whether you can. Still single-armor, which §3.4 wants fixed with a multi-part boss model that does not exist yet.
